mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a risk premium adjustment that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified inflation spike, or CPIAUCSL does not exceed 0.3% in the trigger month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS employment exceeds 5,000 jobs, indicating labor market strengthening, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 5,000 in the current month
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) compared to the pre-trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in RSAFS industrial production of at least 2% signals weakening demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by at least 2% in the current month relative to prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns (aggregated over multiple 5-day windows) are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (≥ 3% month-over-month) reflects supply-side constraints that raise uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by at least 3% in the current month
failure_condition: During the 20-day window following the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5%, the increased discount rate erodes equity present value expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in the current month
failure_condition: The 60-day average 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the high-rate episode.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-week increase in UNRATE above 5.5% suggests rising wage pressures and higher labor costs, which are associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stays above 5.5% for 4 consecutive weeks ending in the current month
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return (p > 0.05) during the 4-week high-unemployment-rate window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly declines in GDPC1 (demand) and HOUST (utilization) of at least 2% each indicate softening economic momentum, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < prev_month by ≥2% AND HOUST < prev_month by ≥2% in the current month
regime_hint: dual softness in demand and utilization
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns (aggregated over multiple 5-day windows) are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the interaction period.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO falls by more than 6% in a month, supply chain disruptions outweigh demand signals, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days in a non-recession regime.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >6% in the current month
failure_condition: During the 20-day window following the trigger, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) despite the supply shock.
